request:
Stop forcing Claude acceptEdits permission mode

## Problem

GitWeave currently launches Claude with:

```text
--permission-mode acceptEdits
```

unconditionally.

This makes GitWeave choose a Claude permission policy even when the graph author did not request one.

The desired baseline for GitWeave is to behave as close as practical to launching Claude normally. GitWeave should not preemptively decide Claude's native permission behavior.

## Expected outcome

Do not force `--permission-mode acceptEdits` by default.

Claude Agent Nodes should use Claude's normal/default automatic permission behavior unless the graph author explicitly requests a provider-specific permission mode.

Conceptually:

```text
Claude node without permission configuration
  → normal Claude permission behavior

Claude node with explicit permission configuration
  → pass that explicit native setting through
```

If the current Claude CLI has a specific mode corresponding to its normal automatic behavior, use that only where needed to preserve ordinary non-interactive execution semantics. Do not introduce a GitWeave-specific permission policy.

Keep permission configuration provider-specific and optional rather than trying to normalize it across Codex and Claude.

## Context

This is the same design direction as #11 for sandboxing:

> Native agent restrictions should not be imposed by GitWeave unless explicitly requested.

The goal is not to remove Claude's native permission system. The goal is for GitWeave to stop selecting a restrictive or permissive policy on the user's behalf by default.


User directive: GitWeave implements, creates a separate PR, reviews/fixes iteratively and merges only when clean. Stop on unsupported operations or permission/allowance limits and ask the user. No parent manual substitute is authorized.
